clue.text: A fan of queen?

parts.note: reads like a devotee of the rock band Queen, but means someone who supports rule by a sovereign

explanation.surface: Someone who loves the band Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital-free 'queen' hides that the band is a red herring: the fan is of the crown.
explanation.definitionFit: A royalist who favours government by a crowned sovereign is literally a fan of the queen.

clue.text: Reversed vehicle into marketplace

indicators.note: Reversed tells us the vehicle word is read backwards

parts.note: a tram is a vehicle running on rails

explanation.surface: A driver backs a van into a market square.
explanation.definitionFit: A mart is a trading place, a synonym of market.

clue.text: Man to show reverence, we hear?

indicators.note: we hear says the word for showing reverence is spoken, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: to kneel is to bow down in respect

explanation.surface: A question about a man paying respects.
explanation.definitionFit: Neil is a man's first name, so the definition is an example.

clue.text: Rebellion from engineers attached to electrical unit

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
the volt is the unit of electrical potential

explanation.surface: An uprising begins among engineers linked to a power unit.
explanation.definitionFit: A revolt is an uprising against authority, the same as a rebellion.

clue.text: The real England's misrepresented in fairy story

indicators.note: misrepresented suggests the letters of the phrase are presented in a different order

explanation.surface: A complaint that a folk tale distorts the true England.
explanation.definitionFit: The tale of two children and a gingerbread witch's house is a classic Grimm fairy tale.

clue.text: Some sissies taking a rest

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Timid people taking a break.
explanation.definitionFit: A siesta is an afternoon nap, a kind of rest.

clue.text: Something overhanging to make one panic

definitions.meaning: a hanging piece of material such as on an envelope or pocket
a state of agitation, as in 'getting in a state'

explanation.surface: An overhang that makes someone nervous.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: a hinged or hanging piece, and a fluster or state of alarm.

clue.text: Idolise Len playing — there's something about his bat?

indicators.note: playing hints the letters of these words are moved around in play

explanation.surface: Fans worship a cricketer called Len as he plays.
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket bats made of willow are traditionally rubbed with this oil to protect them, so it is literally on the bat.
explanation.definitionFit: Flax-seed oil is rubbed into a cricket bat's willow to keep it supple.

clue.text: Colonnades with elegance surrounded by fairies

indicators.note: surrounded by puts the elegance word inside the fairies word

parts.note: peris are fairies or sprites in Persian myth
style means elegance or flair

explanation.surface: Pillared walkways graced by fairies.
explanation.definitionFit: A peristyle is a row of columns round a court, so plural colonnades.

clue.text: Wheel should not need to be restricted — possible safety device included?

definitions.text: Wheel should not need to be

indicators.note: included says the safety device sits inside the word for restricted

parts.note: reined, as a horse is reined in, means held back
a vent can release pressure safely

explanation.surface: An engineering complaint that a wheel needs no restraints, with a safety device fitted.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the saying 'don't reinvent the wheel'.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: repeating needless work is called making the wheel afresh.

clue.text: Roman emperor last to come to the fore as an exceptional person

indicators.text: last to come to the fore
indicators.note: last to come to the fore moves the final letter of the emperor word to its front

parts.note: Nero was the Roman emperor who fiddled while Rome burned

explanation.surface: A Roman emperor moves to the front as a remarkable figure.
explanation.definitionFit: A oner is British slang for a unique or outstanding individual.

clue.text: Daringly innovative lady brought in by professional fellows

parts.note: pro is short for professional

indicators.note: brought in by puts the lady's name within the fellows word

parts.note: men are fellows
Thea is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A bold woman is introduced by a group of professionals.
explanation.definitionFit: After the Titan who stole fire for mankind, the adjective means boldly creative.

clue.text: Leaders in the world of newspapers

definitions.text: Leaders in the world of newspapers

parts.words: Leaders in the world of newspapers
parts.note: reads as top people in journalism, but leaders here are the leading articles of a paper

explanation.definitionFit: A leader in British papers is the leading opinion article, written for the editor.

clue.text: Pound, one found in foreign coins offered by customers

indicators.note: found in puts the pound and one inside the coins

parts.note: cents are coins in many currencies such as the dollar
L is the abbreviation for pound (libra)
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Customers pay with pounds and foreign coins.
explanation.definitionFit: Clients are people who buy services, the same as customers.

clue.text: Succeed but stop bowling?

definitions.meaning: to work out or turn out well
in cricket a bowler taken out of the attack is said to be taken off

explanation.surface: Doing well yet ceasing to bowl in a cricket match.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses of the phrase: work out successfully, and be withdrawn from bowling in cricket.

clue.text: Dreadful clues are deficient, not divine

indicators.note: Dreadful suggests the letters are in a bad state and need reshuffling
deficient means the word lacks its final letter

explanation.surface: A setter is told the clues are terrible and poor, and ungodly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deficient' cuts ARE to AR; 'Dreadful' rearranges CLUES plus AR.
explanation.definitionFit: Secular means worldly rather than religious, the opposite of holy.

clue.text: Poker? One may be that brilliant

definitions.meaning: a fire poker left in the coals glows red
excellent or sensational, as in a top performance

explanation.surface: A fireside poker that could be dazzling.
explanation.definitionFit: A poker left in a fire becomes glowing; slang also uses the phrase for excellent.

clue.text: Famous leader — aged and exceptionally sane

parts.note: AE is the abbreviation for aetatis, meaning aged

indicators.note: exceptionally hints the letters are arranged out of the usual order

explanation.surface: A celebrated chief, old and unusually level-headed.
explanation.definitionFit: The Trojan hero of Virgil's Aeneid led his people to Italy.

clue.text: Occasion for sending greetings card with astounding rhyme possibly

indicators.note: possibly suggests these letters might be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A greetings card bearing a remarkable verse.
explanation.definitionFit: The British name for the day honouring mums, when cards are sent to them.

clue.text: Plant requiring good financial management

definitions.meaning: a pink-flowered coastal plant, also called sea pink

explanation.surface: A plant that demands careful budgeting.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: the sea pink flower, and frugality with money.

clue.text: Story full of dry gossip

indicators.note: full of means the story word contains the dry word

parts.note: a tale is a story
TT means teetotal, i.e. dry

explanation.surface: A tale packed with dull chatter.
explanation.definitionFit: Tattle is idle talk or tittle-tattle, the same as gossip.

clue.text: Spite from male and female

parts.note: Alice is a female name

explanation.surface: Spite coming from a man and a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Malice is the wish to do harm, a synonym of spite.

clue.text: Moody? The Spanish will knock out love music

indicators.note: will knock out says the love letter is removed and replaced by the Spanish word

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A Spaniard spurns love for a moody tune.
explanation.definitionFit: A melody is a tune, a piece of music.

clue.text: Skilled man who could do things on the hoof

definitions.text: Skilled man who could do things on the hoof

parts.words: Skilled man who could do things on the hoof
parts.note: on the hoof usually means improvising, but here it is a horse's hoof being shod

explanation.definitionFit: A blacksmith who shoes horses works literally on their hooves.

clue.text: Times to strike out with no end in sight

indicators.note: with no end in sight means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: to erase is to delete or strike out

explanation.surface: Industrial unrest: periods of striking with no conclusion visible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strike out' suggests walk-outs, but it means delete.
explanation.definitionFit: Eras are periods, as times in history.

clue.text: A sporting occasion one of Arthur's men had missed

indicators.note: missed means the word had is left out

parts.note: Sir Galahad was a Knight of the Round Table
taken as written

explanation.surface: A knight misses a sports day.
explanation.definitionFit: A gala is a festive event, such as a swimming gala.

clue.text: Part of vehicle in ancient city

definitions.meaning: a rubber ring on a wheel
the Phoenician port in modern Lebanon

explanation.surface: A vehicle component found in an old city.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: a wheel's rubber covering, and the ancient Phoenician city.

clue.text: Not moving stuff in the office cupboard when told

indicators.note: when told says the office supplies word is spoken, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: pens, paper and envelopes are office supplies

explanation.surface: Office supplies stay put in the cupboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Stationary means standing still, motionless.

clue.text: Inquisitive and loud? Not I!

indicators.note: Not I tells us the letter I is taken away

parts.note: noisy means loud

explanation.surface: A busybody denies being nosy and noisy.
explanation.definitionFit: Nosy means prying, too curious about others.

clue.text: Last time for exiting from supermarket?

definitions.text: Last time for exiting from supermarket?

parts.words: Last time for exiting from supermarket?
parts.note: reads as the last moment to leave a shop, but is the date stamped on food

explanation.definitionFit: The date printed on goods marks the deadline by which they must leave shop shelves.
